transaction_semantics.admission: Every included EX expression, actual event/frame parameter, current live source identity, target/creation descriptor and operation argument is available before that envelope is enqueued. A future result of another EX inside that envelope is not available.
transaction_semantics.waiting: Missing event values remain in the target Qi_J0 arrival group or a JK readiness structure. There is no incomplete transaction task at a FIFO head, and no additional execution FIFO.
transaction_semantics.zero: A produced zero is available data. READY zero is available control data and rejects an ACK; it is not an ACK waiting instruction.
transaction_semantics.ordinary_q: Actual ordinary Q sources exist before enqueue, and their latest q is read at each EX start. Readiness does not freeze all q. One EX fixes its own source values until it finishes.
transaction_semantics.private_loads: An envelope may carry a fully specified private EX installation and restoration for a concrete target, with all of that EX input values already available. New-node creation initializes declared zero then real EX loads results. Existing final EX is restored; no external intermediate version is exposed. Targets and consumers protected by other tasks may not be rewired/deleted.
transaction_semantics.independence: Sibling EX may share existing inputs. They cannot use each other new results. A completion EX uses existing inputs and publishes only after the full atomic envelope commits.
transaction_semantics.successors: Successor tasks are distinct envelopes. Normal publication or a declared factory request performs their separate admission after the producer has committed. They are never prequeued with future values.
transaction_semantics.factory: Factory operations use already prepared descriptions/identities/locks. They cannot evaluate an implicit EX, write existing q directly, use newly computed primary parity as a parameter, or add a private task queue.
transaction_semantics.commit_order: Execute the explicitly ordered primary and bound EX, then commit all q/structure/operation effects atomically. Register explicit successor requests in the stated order, then publish actual evaluated EX results once; targets from one publication are handled by ascending numeric Q id.
transaction_semantics.initialization: Initialization never publishes. Reserved numeric identifiers are not model Q nodes and do not supply parameter data.
transaction_semantics.generation_protection: Only delete a closed retired fragment after queued primary/auxiliary targets, source versions, arrivals, retained frame/slot dependencies and other real consumers are gone. No exemptions. Partial 8-slot blocks retain all accepted slots; only a full exhausted generation with no dependencies may reuse capacity.

task_shape_revision.planned_creations: Optional complete {node,initial_q,role,condition} descriptors for nodes created by this transaction. They are not currently live and cannot serve as pre-enqueue result sources. Their initial literals and all actual load inputs already exist before admission. A bound EX may target such an explicitly planned node after its creation; it cannot read another new node result.
task_shape_revision.protected_operation_targets: Optional Target list for concrete slot, retention, qualification and request-source objects fixed by an admitted ACK action. These are distinct from the EX-only protected_reads union.
task_shape_revision.operation_parameters: For ACK actions, explicit bound_frame/bound_slot_valid/retention_data/qualification/request_id/request_frame/request_data/next_post_slot_valid/creation_recipe/stale_action. Guards read existing objects once before any business changes; they do not use newly evaluated primary q.
task_shape_revision.bound_ex: Each item contains target Target, expression, parameters, condition, final_ex. It is a real independent JK EX, including a concrete private load+restore when expression differs. Its input sources must all be ready before parent enqueue.
task_shape_revision.parameters: bits plus source-index map plus optional ordered frame projection. A task and each bound EX own their immutable event pools. Ordinary q not present in these pools remains a live read.
task_shape_revision.admission: Descriptive evidence of the existing parameter set. It is neither a runtime gate nor a substitute boolean for JK control.
task_shape_revision.context: Identity metadata only; no extra business bits. ACK successful decoder publication additionally binds its observed qualified FrameRef and concrete operation node refs. No rebinding to another frame.
task_shape_revision.protected_reads: Exact non-self ordinary live-source Target union of primary and bound EX, excluding locked/event values. Binding protects identity/version, not q value.
task_shape_revision.opaque_operations: Consumers must explicitly implement this exact registered contract; unknown operation/profile/revision is rejected, never interpreted as executable code.

CLAIM.boolean: old_C XOR ((NOT old_C) AND PRE.V AND previous.READY) = old_C OR (PRE.V AND previous.READY)
CLAIM.go_final_purpose: Keep the consumed PRE.V a genuine EX source after JOIN deletion; repeated XOR cancels while preserving CLAIM q. PRE.V clear0 publishes nothing.

GO.parameter_policy: JOIN is stateless; lock the published 1 in the GO task

COMP_i.parameter_policy: GO is stateless; lock its 1. PRE.D and previous.S remain ordinary state reads and protected stable identities.

COMMIT.parameter_policy: Each COMP is stateless. Collect both actual 0/1 results before this task exists. Own parity result is observation and is not an operation parameter.

POST_D_and_NEXT_S.parameter_policy: Each independent EX uses its own copy of the already collected COMP_i lock; NEXT.S never reads freshly loaded POST.D.

NEXT_READY.atomic_context: Set together with all independent next-state loads; it reads existing T1, not newly computed next-state values.

READY_OBSERVER.purpose: Real consumer keeps a completed frontier legal when no successor JOIN exists. The READY event produces one actual observation task; A consumes this silent observer.

ordering_requirements: JOIN.id < CLAIM.id for every round; each READY/PRE.V completion publication enqueues JOIN before CLAIM in RAM.FIFO.
Each PRE.V and NEXT.READY is set and publishes exactly once per physical round; initial zero is no event, and later zero clear is filtered by pro=q=1.

All JOIN and CLAIM tasks produced by the two one-shot completion events precede the successful GO task. This is proved by same-source target order and RAM FIFO. GO checks the actual saved dependency set before mutation; if unexpected protection contradicts this admitted profile, reject the candidate operation under the still-pending failure policy, never block a RAM queue head or spin/re-enqueue a not-ready GO. A generalized design must perform waiting before GO admission.
Next-frontier nodes are reserved with initial zero and READY zero at ACCEPT so an early next frame can reference the exact next-state identities without reading them as finished results.
A reserved frontier identity and a completed frontier identity are distinct lifecycle metadata; no duplicate business readiness boolean is introduced.

readiness_construction.completion_token_EX: J0K(S)K(S)K1 is a real stateless JK EX. The two reads of the same already-ready S cancel, so both S=0 and S=1 produce event 1.
readiness_construction.independent_same_transaction: B and E_B both read existing D. R and E_R both read existing B or H. R_FRAME and E_M both read existing MODE. No completion token reads the primary node result. Commit atomically completes both EX before publishing the token through ordinary pro.
readiness_construction.not_a_fabricated_event: Only the registered real EX evaluation publishes its own result. RAM.FACTORY never synthesizes a Q event or writes an existing q. An aborted transaction publishes no completion event.
readiness_construction.no_duplicate_aux_tasks: E_B does not reference ESTART, E_R does not reference G_B or ESTART, and E_M does not reference R_FRAME. Those sources would cause unintended ordinary tasks or create new dependencies. Their actual ordinary sources stay quiet.
readiness_construction.join: Each target waits for all distinct stateless token events, locks their data and clears that arrival group on task formation under the existing Qi_J0 rule.
readiness_construction.LATCH_reference: LATCH is quiet stateful and has a genuine A consumer from creation until cleanup. Its EX additionally consumes ESTART and, for first requests, G_B; thus dormant pipeline stateless tails already have real consumers before the fixed nodes are connected. Active R_FRAME also contains K(LATCH) twice; this initialized q is transparent and is never presented as a completion flag.
readiness_construction.zero_is_not_missing: All completion tokens publish 1 for either data value. Eligibility is based on completion events, not truthiness of data bits.
readiness_construction.quiet_primary_reason: B must not publish: H and A would otherwise receive ordinary triggers. R must not publish: fixed O would otherwise enqueue before the batch lock. The explicit auxiliary token EX publish while these primary nodes stay quiet.
readiness_construction.admission: The real stateless ADMIT_GATE reads BUSY and CLAIM. Only the existing business request head can be attempted. G and its independent CLAIM EX commit atomically. A q=1 event forms START through ordinary Qi_J0 triggering; the claim makes duplicate attempts harmless without a hidden Boolean.
readiness_construction.LATCH_arrival_state: ESTART may be recorded before any B/R task completes; G_B may be recorded before any R task completes. Snapshots must retain these partial target-specific arrivals with the actual source identity and data. The extra inputs do not add task executions.

LATCH.primary_EX: LATCH computes AND of its already-latched completion/admission-stage values; the result is not an input parameter of its operations.
operations_in_order: Read already-produced Q53,Q54,Q61 and create independently locked output parameters.

Prepare idle EX restoration and reference detachment; deletion of transient request nodes, including this LATCH, occurs only at the final atomic commit after the completed-primary/no-publication/no-other-dependency conditions in cleanup.current_LATCH_final_commit_rule are met.

After batch output locking and BUSY clear commit, remove this request from the business request list. Only then may the next request head have its real G admission task requested. That G evaluates its own ready BUSY/CLAIM parameters; no next K/MODE computation occurs inside LATCH.
LATCH.no_intermediate_dependency: Every output bit is read from a prior completed task. The marker is not taken from a new result produced inside LATCH.
LATCH.deletion_boundary: No node is removed while its own EX or a later dependent step remains unfinished. The final commit may simultaneously settle the fully evaluated quiet LATCH task and delete its now-unneeded transient target.

ADMIT_GATE.proof: Both EX consume pre-existing BUSY; G additionally consumes old CLAIM. CLAIM never reads G result. G is evaluated before CLAIM changes, and BUSY is unchanged.
ADMIT_GATE.commit: Publish G only if its already computed result is 1. Its real START consumer creates the START task.
ADMIT_GATE.source_rule: Factory only requests a real G task for the eligible request identity; it does not manufacture the G event or the START task.

cleanup.q_preservation: Restoring EX does not evaluate it and does not overwrite B, R or R_FRAME q. B retains first-frame data until guarded FRAME_OUT captures H.
cleanup.A: Remove every deleted request K/START/LATCH/CLAIM reference; do not evaluate A or A_READ. Other live upstream stateful references remain. Remove the temporary request graph only after all active target/source/arrival dependencies are gone.
deletion_preconditions: No duplicate G admission task, queued START task or other active dependency still targets this request G/CLAIM/START. A duplicate pending G must finish (emitting nothing) before its target can be deleted; do not silently remove a queued task.
All B/R/marker tasks in this preparation have completed.
All token arrival groups used by G_B/LATCH have been consumed into completed tasks.
No remaining task target, ordinary source, bound auxiliary target, arrival group or structural consumer protects a deleted node.
Every retained Q still has legal true EX sources and at least one true EX/q_y consumer.
cleanup.frozen_output_tasks: New output tasks use their own locked Q53,Q54,Q61 values. Later changes of those sources do not alter the old tasks. Their fixed output targets remain protected.
cleanup.first_FRAME_OUT_dependencies: Bind H0/H1, CACHE, READY and F targets plus their actual ordinary sources at output enqueue after cleanup EX versions are final. Protect B sources until first FRAME_OUT completes.

current_LATCH_final_commit_rule.allowed_boundary: Deletion of this request LATCH is committed only at the final atomic task commit, never during an active LATCH EX or an unfinished parameter read.
must_already_be_finished: The current LATCH primary has completed its complete EX and its final parameter read.
Its target arrival group was moved into this task and has been consumed.
LATCH is quiet, so there is no current LATCH result publication still needing its identity.
The independent bound BUSY EX has completed; it does not read LATCH.
The output parameter arrays were already independently locked from previously produced R and R_FRAME values.
All fixed EX and A references to removed nodes have been atomically detached or restored.
No other queued primary/auxiliary task, source protection, unconsumed arrival or structural consumer still needs any node being deleted.
current_LATCH_final_commit_rule.commit: After these checks the one complete atomic commit may remove the transient request nodes and settle the current task together. The visible checkpoint contains neither a half-executed task nor a partly removed graph.
current_LATCH_final_commit_rule.not_an_exemption: The currently completed primary no longer has an unfinished dependency on its target at this final commit. This does not exempt the target from source/consumer rules while it is live and does not permit deleting any still-needed current or later object.
current_LATCH_final_commit_rule.if_still_needed: If the current task still needs LATCH for a later EX, publication or operation, or another dependency survives, preserve LATCH and its required closed fragment for a later safe retirement transaction.

first_independent_EX_order: Q47 executes J0K1K(Q45)K(Q46) BEFORE Q45 changes

not_EX_edges: B primary shares a transaction with E_B
R primary shares a transaction with E_R
R_FRAME primary shares a transaction with E_M
static_graph_reasoning.no_cycle_argument: There is no R→E_R or R_FRAME→E_M EX edge. E_R reads B/H and E_M reads MODE, so E_R/E_M→LATCH→A→A_READ→R has no return edge. LATCH also feeds R_FRAME transparently. Pending pipeline ESTART/G_B/ER/EM already feed LATCH, and quiet LATCH feeds A. G feeds START, CLAIM feeds G, and START feeds A. BUSY only reads T1. Thus both pending and active graphs have genuine consumers without a multi-node EX cycle.
forbidden_shortcuts: Do not create done events without evaluating the corresponding completion EX.

Do not lock the outputs inside the transaction that first creates R_FRAME.q.
Do not add E_B/E_R/E_M/ESTART/G_B to A; stateless publication must not inadvertently create A tasks.
Do not give B/R default pro merely to obtain a completion event.

replay_action.ordering: 加入原有业务输出准备请求序列，不新建执行FIFO；输出阶段依其真实就绪结构另行入队。
replay_action.on_later_consumption: 已完成中转锁存的重发输出继续使用自己的输出任务参数；旧重发FRAME_OUT不得建立或恢复ACK资格。

structural_closure.A: Q51.EX = J0 followed by one K for each live quiet stateful Q in Q10..Q50 or Q>=71, in numeric order. Publishing PRE.V/READY have CLAIM/observer consumers, never A. Q51/Q52 keep their actual initialized q=0 and are not executed as a checksum in this design. R reads Q52 twice transparently.
structural_closure.PRE_V_after_GO: CLAIM final hold EX retains K(PRE.V) twice so the spent PRE.V remains genuinely referenced even after JOIN retirement. No event on clear-to-zero under pro=q=1.
structural_closure.DAG: All real EX edges, including quiet and transparent reads, participate; exclude only legal stateful self edges.

definition.operation_argument_readiness: A structural operation may take an already existing module/container identity and a complete mutation description; it operates on that current object atomically. Concrete included EX targets and all data inputs must already be bound, or be explicit new-target creation descriptors with known initial literals and independent existing load inputs. Do not use a mutable container reference to disguise a missing business result.
